opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nancy Hunter (employee ID E038) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E038.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nancy Hunter (E038) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, not the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for full-time employees here. Maximum allowed is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E038 (Nancy Hunter) is a contractor with basic security training, which conflicts with the prior HR note listing her as full-time. Under policy, contractors max out at read (write only with advanced training; never admin). Since she requested admin, the maximum allowed is read. Recommend granting read.
reason: Nancy Hunter (E038) requested admin access to Payroll. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR lists her as full-time (max write for Payroll, since Engineer does not own Payroll), while Security DB lists her as a contractor with basic security training (max read; write requires advanced training, and contractors are never admin). Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive, security-sourced interpretation: contractor with basic training, whose maximum is read. Since requested admin exceeds read, grant read.
